claims.text: The optimal objective value of the demographic parity adversary upper-bounds the demographic parity distance of any classifier learned from the representation.
The optimal objective value of the equalized odds adversary upper-bounds the equalized odds distance of any classifier learned from the representation.
Cross-entropy adversarial loss biases the adversary toward predicting the majority class when the sensitive attribute is imbalanced, failing to maximize test discrepancy.
LAFTR representations reduce equalized odds unfairness (Delta EO) by an average of approximately 20% relative to a baseline unfair model across 10 transfer tasks on the Heritage Health dataset.
LAFTR achieves the lowest equalized odds unfairness on 7 out of 10 transfer tasks on the Heritage Health dataset.
LAFTR achieves a lower Maximum Mean Discrepancy (2.7e-5) and lower adversarial sensitive-attribute prediction accuracy (0.761) compared to transfer baselines on the Heritage Health dataset.

evidence.description: Theorem 5.1 proof demonstrates L_Adv^DP(h*) >= Delta_DP(g) where h* is the optimal adversary and g is any classifier operating on representation Z.
Theorem 5.2 proof demonstrates L_Adv^EO(h*) >= Delta_EO(g) where h* is the optimal adversary taking both Z and label Y as inputs.

Appendix A presents a synthetic binary example where cross-entropy loss assigns every sample to the majority group (A=0), yielding zero test discrepancy, whereas group-normalized L1 yields test discrepancy 0.368.
Figure 3 shows an average relative reduction of ~20% in Delta EO across 10 transfer tasks compared to the Target-Unfair baseline.
Table 1 shows LAFTR achieves the lowest Delta EO on tasks MSC2, ARTHSPIN, NEUMENT, RESPR4, MISCHRT, SKNAUT, and GIBLEED out of 10 primary condition group transfer tasks.
Table 2 reports LAFTR MMD as 2.7e-5 compared to 1.1e-2 for Transfer-Unfair and 1.4e-3 for Transfer-Fair, with adversarial accuracy of 0.761 compared to 0.784-0.787 for baselines.

methodologies.name: Learned Adversarially Fair and Transferable Representations (LAFTR)
methodologies.description: An adversarial representation learning framework optimizing an encoder, classifier, decoder, and adversary using group-normalized L1 losses tied to specific group fairness metrics.

limitations.text: Optimizing group-normalized L1 loss with gradients in adversarial training can be difficult and exhibits training instability.
Satisfying group fairness constraints conflicts with learning well-calibrated classifiers.
Demographic parity has limited usefulness when the base rates between groups differ in the ground truth labels.

future_work.text: Perform an in-depth comparison between adversarial and non-adversarial fair representation learning methods such as MMD.
Investigate optimal continuous relaxation adversarial loss functions to stabilize adversarial training of fair representations.
Understand between what tasks and in what conditions transfer fairness is possible and most likely to succeed.
